### Cause & Effect Sentence Stem Bank 因果与反驳句式库 *(Must use at least 2 stems 至少使用 2 个句式)*

- **Grade 6/7 Stems:**
  - *Because* `[Geographic Feature/Challenge]`, *the society* `[Effect/Solution]`...
  - *Due to* `[Environmental Condition]`, `[Historical Outcome]` *gradually occurred over time...*
  - `[Environmental Factor]` *was a significant factor; as a result,* `[Civilization Effect]`...
  - `[Challenge]` *created a need for* `[Innovation]`; *consequently,* `[Action taken]`...
- **Grade 8 Stems:**
  - *Stemming from* `[Geographic Advantage/Disadvantage]`, *the community experienced* `[Systemic Effect]`...
  - `[Environmental/Political Factor]` *fundamentally altered* `[Social System]`, *thus allowing for* `[Outcome]`...
- **Counter-Argument Stems (Required 必选反驳句式):**
  - *While* `[Other Civilization]` *offered* `[Positive Feature]`, *we chose* `[Our Civilization]` *because* `[Key Reason]`...
  - *Unlike* `[Other Civilization]` *which suffered from* `[Specific Problem]`, *our choice provided* `[Specific Benefit]`...

## Teacher Answer Key & Lesson Plan 教师答案与教案

### Completed 3-Civilization Comparison Matrix (Answer Key)

| Dimension / Category | Mesopotamia (Tigris & Euphrates) | Ancient Egypt (Nile River) | Indus Valley (Indus & Ganges) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1. Geography & Environment**<br>*(Rivers, Flooding & Barriers)* | • **Rivers:** Tigris & Euphrates<br>• **Flooding:** Unpredictable & violent; left fertile {{< vocab "silt" >}}<br>• **Barriers:** NO natural barriers (open plain; vulnerable to invasion) | • **River:** Nile (flows north to {{< vocab "delta" >}})<br>• **Flooding:** Predictable (July–Oct); rich black silt<br>• **Barriers:** Vast deserts & seas on both sides (highly secure) | • **Rivers:** Indus & Ganges ({{< vocab "Indo-Gangetic Plain" >}})<br>• **Climate:** Seasonal {{< vocab "monsoon" text="monsoons" >}} (wet summer / dry winter)<br>• **Barriers:** Himalayas, Hindu Kush & Karakorum mountains |
| **2. Belief Systems & Afterlife**<br>*(Gods, Worldview & Tombs)* | • **Religion:** {{< vocab "polytheism" text="Polytheistic" >}} (2,000+ gods; Enlil = storm god)<br>• **View of Deities:** Powerful, unpredictable & angry<br>• **Afterlife:** Gloomy "land of no return" (souls eat dust) | • **Religion:** Polytheistic (Re, Osiris, Isis; {{< vocab "pharaoh" >}} = living god)<br>• **Afterlife:** Beautiful Other World ({{< vocab "ka" >}} preserved via {{< vocab "mummification" >}})<br>• **Tombs:** Monumental {{< vocab "pyramid" text="Pyramids" >}} | • **Religion:** Polytheistic links to early Hinduism (Shiva, mother goddess, bull worship)<br>• **Society:** Relatively peaceful (few weapons; clay/wooden toys found) |
| **3. Inventions & Innovations**<br>*(Writing, Tech & Science)* | • **Writing:** {{< vocab "cuneiform" text="Cuneiform" >}} on clay tablets<br>• **Innovations:** Wheel, sail, plow, bronze, base-60 math (60 sec/min, 360° circle)<br>• **Architecture:** {{< vocab "ziggurat" text="Ziggurats" >}}, arches, mud-brick walls | • **Writing:** {{< vocab "hieroglyphics" text="Hieroglyphics" >}} on {{< vocab "papyrus" >}} ({{< vocab "Rosetta Stone" >}} key)<br>• **Tech:** 365-day solar calendar, geometry, advanced medicine (pulse, splints, surgery) | • **Writing:** Undeciphered script (~400 symbols on {{< vocab "Harappan seals" text="seals" >}})<br>• **City Planning:** Precise {{< vocab "grid system" >}}, fortified {{< vocab "citadel" >}}, standard oven-baked bricks, private bathrooms & brick sewers |
| **4. Social & Political Order**<br>*(Government, Laws & Hierarchy)* | • **Government:** Independent {{< vocab "city-state" text="city-states" >}} → {{< vocab "dynasty" text="Dynasties" >}} → {{< vocab "empire" text="Empires" >}} (Sargon, Hammurabi)<br>• **Laws:** {{< vocab "Code of Hammurabi" >}} (282 laws; stratified justice) | • **Government:** Unified Kingdom under Pharaoh ({{< vocab "theocracy" >}}; 31 dynasties; capital Memphis)<br>• **Social Structure:** Social pyramid; social mobility via literacy; women held property/divorce rights | • **Government:** Strong central government (indicated by uniform bricks, streets, and drains across cities)<br>• **Decline:** Tectonic shifts (earthquakes/floods/river shift), soil exhaustion, Aryan migration |

### 50-Minute Review Lesson Flow (Mingwan School Lesson Plan)

1. **Stage 1 · Hook & Framing: Where Would You Settle? (7 min):**
   - *Hook (2 min):* Project the 2500 B.C. time-travel prompt.
   - *Direct Framing (2 min):* Explain the collaborative comparison matrix and the "River Valley Immigrant Pitch" challenge.
   - *Role Assignment (3 min):* Assign Scribe, Map Specialist, Researcher, and Presenter.
2. **Stage 2 · Collaborative Practice: 3-Civilization Matrix (18 min):**
   - *Group Matrix Work (15 min):* Table groups use their Reading Packets (Lessons 1, 3, and 4) to fill in all 4 dimensions of the matrix.
   - *Teacher Circulation (3 min):* Verify that students distinguish between unpredictable Tigris/Euphrates floods and predictable Nile floods, and note Harappan grid planning vs. Mesopotamian winding streets.
3. **Stage 3 · Decision & Synthesis: Group Choice & Argument (15 min):**
   - *Group Decision (3 min):* Table groups vote on ONE river civilization to settle in.
   - *Argument Construction (12 min):* Scribes draft a 5–7 sentence argument using at least 2 historical facts, 2 cause-and-effect stems, and a counter-argument addressing another civilization.
4. **Stage 4 · Group Presentations: The Immigrant Pitch (7 min):**
   - *Speedy Pitch Showcase (5 min):* 3 selected Spokespersons deliver a 60-second pitch defending their chosen civilization.
   - *Peer Verification (2 min):* Classmates verify the pitch using the Part 3 checklist.
5. **Stage 5 · Closure & Self-Check (3 min):**
   - Students complete the self-check checklist and turn in their sheets.
:::
